title: Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo announce September 15-16 joint online-only auction
summary: Artemis Fine Arts in association with Arte Primitivo will present an online-only auction September 15-16 featuring Pre-Columbian, Native American, and fossils on Day 1 , followed by Classical and Near Eastern antiquities, Tribal, African, and Asian art on Day 2 . The jointly-produced auction draws on decades of experience and expertise from both galleries. The principals remain committed to maintaining the same high standards, connoisseurship, and client service that collectors have come to expect of both of the firms. title: China Institute Gallery at 60, 1966-2026: Selections from Three Millennia of Chinese Art
summary: For six decades, China Institute Gallery has quietly informed the way Americans see Chinese art. Since opening in 1966 as the first nonprofit gallery in the United States devoted exclusively to Chinese art, it has introduced generations of audiences to extraordinary works spanning thousands of years, presenting pioneering exhibitions that brought masterpieces to the United States for the first time or featured works that had never before been seen outside China. This fall, as China Institute of America celebrates its Centennial and the Gallery marks its 60th anniversary, a new exhibition looks back at that remarkable legacy. China Institute Gallery at 60, 1966-2026: Selections from Three Millennia of Chinese Art, presents both a celebration of Chinese artistic achievement and a reflection on the institution that helped shape the study and appreciation of Chinese

title: SJ Auctioneers announces online-only Estate Silverware, Toys, Décor & Glass Art auction
summary: Outstanding sterling silver flatware sets and individual pieces will take center stage in SJ Auctioneers’ online-only Estate Silverware, Toys, Décor & Glass Art auction slated for Sunday, October 18th, beginning promptly at 6pm Eastern time. Of the 20 expected top lots, fully 15 are sterling silver, a category for which SJ Auctioneers has become rather famous. The auction, with 281 quality lots, is live now, on LiveAuctioneers.com. The catalog is filled with world-famous artists, designers and silversmiths, names such as Kirk, Alexander Macrae, Buccellati, Pampaloni, Gorham, David Webb, Tiffany & Co., David Yurman, International Sterling, Marco Bicego, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Nintendo, Herend, Disney, Dinky, Mojo Lesney, Limoges, Steuben, Baccarat, Lalique, Cartier, ST DuPont, and many others. summary: An important museum-quality collection of over 240 Victorian Hair Combs, Hair Pins and Ornaments, all from a private collector, will be presented at Roland Auctions NY upcoming Saturday, September 19th auction at 10am. Of course, Fine and Contemporary Art, Sculpture, Decorative Arts, Antique and Mid-Century Modern furniture, Silver, Asian Art, Rugs, Jewelry and Lighting, along with a beautiful selection of works by Louis Comfort Tiffany will all be represented at the multi-estates auction. Previews for the September 19th auction will be held on Thursday, September 17th and Friday, September 18th from 10am until 6pm. Rarely does one find a collection spanning the years from the late 1700s to the present that includes English, French, American, Spanish and Japanese examples. title: Americas Society opens Telenovela exhibition exploring Latin American pop culture
summary: Opening at Americas Society on September 9, 2026, the exhibition Telenovela explores how contemporary Latinx and Latin American artists have engaged with the visual and conceptual richness of telenovelas, the most circulated Latino cultural product of the postwar period. The exhibition aims to demonstrate that telenovelas are an enduring Pan-American phenomenon that transcends geography, social stratification, or cultural categories. Curated by Aimé Iglesias Lukin, director and chief curator of Art at Americas Society, the show explores the profound cultural, social, and political significance of the telenovela across the Western Hemisphere, positioning it as a serious subject of art-historical inquiry. title: Borusan Contemporary opens its new season with two parallel exhibitions: Time Space Geometry and Haunted
summary: Borusan Contemporary opens its new season with two exhibitions running in parallel at Perili Köşk (the Haunted Mansion), its historic home overlooking the Bosphorus: Olivo Barbieri's Time Space Geometry, the Italian photographer's first solo exhibition in Türkiye, and Haunted, a collection exhibition exploring how artificial intelligence and digital culture are transforming contemporary visual culture. Curated by Fırat Arapoğlu, Time Space Geometry brings together a selection from five thematic series spanning more than two decades of Olivo Barbieri's practice — Time Space Geometry, site specific_, The Waterfall Project, Alps – Geographies and People, and Capri — known for his distinctive use of optical intervention to shift scale, perspective and the perception of place. title: Kunstverein presents group exhibition I, etcetera exploring artistic subjectivity
summary: At the center of the group exhibition I, etcetera is an engagement with artistic subjectivity as always processual and relational. From this premise, the exhibition also turns its attention to the host institution itself, considering the ways in which the Kunstverein assumes and articulates a subjectivity of its own. It asks how narrative strategies and speculative propositions, operating across artistic practices and institutional(ized) processes alike, participate in producing the relations through which the self takes form. The project brings together new commissions and existing works by an intergenerational group of artists, in whose practices interiors, facades, and landscapes recur in both actual and metaphorical forms: as buildings and psychic states, imaginaries and projections, bodies and social spaces. title: NYU's Grey Art Museum presents first comprehensive retrospective of Alison Knowles
summary: This fall the Grey Art Museum at New York University will present by Alison Knowles: A Retrospective (1960–2022), the first comprehensive exhibition of the influential artist’s six-decade career. Best known as a founding member of the interdisciplinary art collective Fluxus, Alison Knowles (1933–2025) was an important figure in the avant-garde community for more than half a century, collaborating with George Brecht, John Cage, Charlotte Moorman, Nam June Paik, Robert Watts, Emmett Williams, and many other artists. On view from September 9, 2026, through January 30, 2027, at 18 Cooper Square, the exhibition is accompanied by the first major catalogue to focus on Knowles’s life and artistic practice, featuring new research on the artist and the history of Fluxus. Organized by the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA) and guest curated by independent curator Karen Moss, the retrospective includes some two hundred objects

title: Rebecca Morgan explores political turmoil and art history in sixth solo show
summary: Asya Geisberg Gallery presents ”Painting in the Apocalypse,” an exhibition of paintings by Rebecca Morgan. In her sixth show with the gallery, Morgan asks how to present images in the face of a raging political landscape. She engages potent themes from all her eras: sympathy for her rural background, feminist reappraisal of art history, and an unbridled excitement at infusing humor and technical prowess into her unabashed critique. Here she sharpens the political content by making it more specific and savage. Haunting images, circling obsessively in Morgan’s mind’s-eye, find their way to fruition in a variety of painterly languages. Morgan's strategic reimagining of art history suggests a possible coping mechanism. The titular artwork, “Painting in the Apocalypse,” inspired by Norman Rockwell’s “Triple Self-Portrait,” adds to prior Morgan themes of paintings within a painting. title: Kunstmuseum Ravensburg brings Expressionism into dialogue with contemporary art in "Questions of Our Time"
summary: What happens when the ideals of German Expressionism are examined from the vantage point of the present? At Kunstmuseum Ravensburg, an exhibition that opened on August 8 brings works from the museum’s Selinka Collection face to face with contemporary artists to explore how questions surrounding the body, gender, nature, consumption, war and cultural identity have changed—and how stubbornly some of them have endured. On view through November 15, 2026, “Questions of Our Time: The Collection Meets the Present” (Zeitfragen. Sammlung trifft Gegenwart) pairs historical works with pieces by contemporary artists across six thematic groupings. title: Derek Eller Gallery presents Julia Bland solo exhibition If Blue is a Holy Color
summary: Derek Eller Gallery will present a solo show of new work by Julia Bland entitled If Blue is a Holy Color. This exhibition will feature textile-painting hybrids and hanging sculptures, which Bland creates through a process of hand-weaving, dying, braiding, embroidering, painting, and embedding with personal fabrics. A video shot in 8mm film depicts process as both ritual and narrative. The architecture of Bland’s composition emerges through an intuitive process of assembly, de-assembly, gathering, and sorting. Structure, composition, geometry and pattern accumulate into recognizable form. Woven patterns in pastel colors evoke the cheery gingham of a picnic blanket and the hard-edged grid, a trope of abstract painting. title: Artcurial expands to the United States
summary: Artcurial continues its international expansion with the opening of a US subsidiary, headquartered in Miami’s Design District. This expansion builds on the house’s international development, already established in Paris, Monaco, Marrakech, and Switzerland. By establishing itself in the world’s leading market for art, collectible automobiles, and luxury goods, Artcurial affirms its ambition to deploy its expertise and know-how there, offering auctions and tailored services to its clientele across the Atlantic. It is in Miami, at the heart of the city’s vibrant automotive and lifestyle scene, that Artcurial will launch its American activities with its Artcurial Motorcars department. Mark your calendars for February 19, 2027, for Miami Sunset Super Cars, Artcurial’s inaugural American sale, to be held at the Hangar at Regatta Harbour, in the Coconut Grove neighborhood, at the heart of the Miami Concours and Moda Miami calendar. title: Fondation d'entreprise Hermès presents Île/Mer/Froid exhibition at La Verrière
summary: From 10 September to 14 November 2026, the Fondation d’entreprise Hermès will present the first personal exhibition dedicated to the French duo Île/Mer/Froid in Belgium. Sculptures, ceramics, woodworks and textiles will inhabit the space in an exhibition composed of a central installation and around fifty other works, the majority of which will be specially produced for the occasion. At La Verrière, they create a whole, and are accompanied by works by ceramicist Richard Dewar, sculptors Daniel Dewar & Grégory Gicquel, photographer Marianne Marić and painter Julien Meert. title: Janet Biggs explores solar eclipses and human perception in new video installations
summary: Cristin Tierney Gallery will present Path of Totality, a solo exhibition of new and recent video installations by Janet Biggs. This is the artist's third solo show with the gallery. The exhibition opens Wednesday, September 9th and will be on view through Saturday, October 24th. For decades, Biggs has traveled to extreme environments, using the journey as a framework to explore how physical landscapes mirror the psychological and emotional terrain of human life. Path of Totality extends this inquiry by bringing together two video installations set in vastly different environments: Eclipse (Antarctica, December 4, 2021), 2022–24, and Eclipse (Amazon, September 7, 1858), 2025. Through a juxtaposition of contemporary footage with historical writings, navigational accounts, and inherited memory, Biggs collapses geographical and temporal distance. The

title: Howard Smith survey at Jane Lombard Gallery explores five decades of abstraction
summary: Jane Lombard Gallery will present Tomorrow isn't Yesterday, a solo exhibition of new and historical works by Howard Smith. Spanning more than five decades, the exhibition examines Smith’s sustained investigation into the singular brushstroke, the painted and unpainted ground, and the capacity of color to shape light and perception. Rather than presenting a chronological survey or tracing the evolution of a style, Tomorrow isn't Yesterday reveals how these fundamental concerns continue to generate new formal capabilities. Reflecting its title, the exhibition considers painting as an ongoing process in which each work emerges through a dialogue between what has come before and what remains possible. At the core of Smith’s practice is the brushstroke, where hand, eye, material, and imagination converge. Working entirely freehand,

title: Fridman Gallery presents Dindga McCannon solo exhibition Yesterday and Today
summary: Fridman Gallery presents Dindga McCannon’s second solo exhibition, Yesterday and Today, which brings together, for the first time, her groundbreaking mixed-media quilts, paintings, and prints, spanning the 1970s to the present day. On her 18th birthday, Dindga went to see a concert in Tompkins Square Park, where she encountered Sun Ra Arkestra, an alternative band whose performance became a kind of epiphany. That encounter shaped the course of her life and artistic process, cementing music as inseparable from her visual language. Her works emerge intuitively and are in many ways improvised akin to a jazz riff. Born and raised in Harlem and the Bronx, Dindga came of age as an artist and young mother during the rise of the civil rights movement. title: Stanley Whitney debuts new and recent paintings at Gagosian in Hong Kong
summary: Gagosian announces Isn’t Love the Strangest Thing, an exhibition of new and recent paintings by Stanley Whitney opening at the gallery in Hong Kong on September 10. This is Whitney’s first solo exhibition in Asia. Isn’t Love the Strangest Thing, which features paintings at a variety of scales, from twelve to seventy-two inches square, is named for a jazz standard recorded by Duke Ellington and His Orchestra in 1936, with vocals by Ivie Anderson. This playful song about the unpredictability of romance explores the ways in which falling in love so often entails a disorienting mixture of joy and sorrow. Whitney’s characteristically vibrant abstractions with their heightened awareness of color offer a visual counterpart to the sense of intoxication the song describes. title: Miles McEnery Gallery showcases twenty-five new single format works by Roy Dowell
summary: Roy Dowell’s solo exhibition Evidence to the Contrary, showcases twenty-five new single format works composed of vinyl emulsion on linen over panels. The works are meditations on Dowell’s personal cabinet of curiosities, his memory of objects, and living between Mexico City and Los Angeles. Dowell is drawn to this specific medium because it allows each layer of the painting to remain fully visible. By eliminating the concealment typical of the creative process, the work achieves a transcendence of time. While each work shares the same dimensions at twenty-four by eighteen inches, the only other unifying feature that links them is Dowell’s artistic intent. He approaches the creation of each work as an individual, self determining endeavor; resulting in a unique, precious object. Dowell shares in the essay, “An Inventory

title: Alexander Gray Associates presents tribute exhibition to late sculptor Melvin Edwards
summary: Alexander Gray Associates presents People Make Art: A Tribute to Melvin Edwards, an exhibition that explores the life and practice of the acclaimed sculptor through the work of fifteen artists who knew him. Rather than attempting to define the full scope of Edwards’s (b.1937, Houston, TX; d.2026, Baltimore, MD) artistic community, the show traces one constellation within a far larger universe of relationships, illuminating the generosity, curiosity, and spirit of exchange that animated his work for more than six decades. Featuring paintings, sculptures, and works on paper from 1954 to 2024, People Make Art reflects the extraordinary breadth of Edwards’s artistic engagement and the enduring vitality of his artistic community. The exhibition takes its title from one of Edwards’s characteristically direct observations: “Art doesn't make art, people make art.”

title: Alexander Berggruen presents Danny Fox's second solo exhibition in New York
summary: Alexander Berggruen presents Danny Fox: Fata Morgana, the gallery’s second solo exhibition with the artist. This exhibition will open Wednesday, September 9 with a 6-8 pm reception at the gallery (1018 Madison Avenue, Floor 3, New York, NY). Danny Fox blends domestic imagery with influences from his natural environment to create eerily striking articulations of the human psyche. His new body of work Fata Morgana explores illusion through optical distortions, ambiguous imagery, and abstracted depth. Across Fox’s recurrent motifs of horses, boats, and interiors, the artist hints at unseen forces of psychology, evident in the figures’ gestures and how they relate to their environments. title: Jack Shainman Gallery presents Becky Suss exhibition Night House
summary: Jack Shainman Gallery presents Night House, an exhibition of new work by Becky Suss that continues her exploration of interiority, domesticity and memory. Through paintings of imagined spaces and intimate vignettes, the exhibition marks a departure for Suss in her use of the darkness and quietude of the night as a lens through which to consider the emotional and psychological resonance of space. Suffused with the kind of specificity of detail that comes from the act of remembrance, Suss’ paintings reclaim the night not only as a time of reflection, but as one where perception deepens and self-knowledge can be pursued. title: Southbank Centre announces lineup for Creative Intelligence weekend takeover
summary: The Southbank Centre today announces further programming for the inaugural edition of Creative Intelligence, a brand new weekend-long takeover exploring the future of art, technology and creativity. The weekend is a highlight of the Southbank Centre’s 75th year, and celebrates the same spirit of innovation and curiosity which launched the 1951 Festival of Britain, the first chapter in the Southbank Centre’s story. Creative Intelligence will take over the Southbank Centre’s iconic 11-acre site from Friday 11 – Sunday 13 September, transforming it into a playground of human imagination: an open and democratic space for learning, play and technological experimentation. The three day programme is packed with art, performance, music, and debate, alongside plenty of opportunities to get hands-on with creative tech. Centred on innovation and discovery

title: RR Auction features Hiroshima flight logbook in Remarkable Rarities sale
summary: From a handwritten account composed aboard the Enola Gay during the Hiroshima atomic bombing mission to Pierre de Coubertin’s working plan for reviving the Olympic Games, RR Auction’s September 2026 Remarkable Rarities sale brings together manuscripts and artifacts tied to consequential moments across modern history. At the center of the sale is Capt. Robert A. Lewis’s mission-used flight logbook from the Enola Gay, containing 25 handwritten pages, including an eight-page account written aboard the aircraft as the Hiroshima mission unfolded on Aug. 6, 1945. Lewis, the Enola Gay’s co-pilot, began his diary with the preflight briefing and takeoff from Tinian and continued recording events as the aircraft approached its target. title: The Southbank Centre presents the UK premiere of Playing With Fire: An Immersive Odyssey with Yuja Wang
summary: This autumn, the Southbank Centre unveils the UK premiere of Playing With Fire: An Immersive Odyssey with Yuja Wang, a major new mixed-reality experience and bold expansion of the piano recital, written and directed by Pierre-Alain Giraud. Combining live recital, visual art, mixed reality and virtual reality technologies with spatialised sound, the production places classical music in striking dialogue with virtual worlds, allowing an unprecedented perspective on the performance of one of the world’s greatest living pianists.
